iterations.theme: Zašto ići na ispovijed ako ćeš opet sagriješiti? Kateheza patera Sebastiana Šujevića o sakramentu ispovijedi kao susretu s milosrdnim Ocem

sections.subtitle: Ući u ispovijed s maštom: sakrament kao živi susret s Bogom
sections.screenshot_description: Pater Sebastian Šujević poziva okupljene da večeras u sakrament ispovijedi uđu s maštom
sections.content:
Katehezu u sklopu ciklusa **DDV kateheza** na kanalu budiFRAjer pater **Sebastian Šujević** otvara podsjetnikom na ono čime je čovjek obdaren: razumom, pameću, pamćenjem, slobodnom voljom i srcem, ali i **maštom**. Upravo preko svih tih sposobnosti, ističe, Gospodin otkriva samoga sebe, progovara čovjeku, potiče ga i omogućuje susret s njim.

Temeljna misao od koje polazi jest da je **svaki sakrament prije svega susret**, i to „duboki susret sa živim Bogom“. Zato slušatelje poziva da večeras u sakrament ispovijedi uđu upravo s maštom, s očekivanjem i otvorenošću. Predlaže im da u srcu nose jednostavno pitanje: *što će mi novo Gospodin dati u sljedećoj ispovijedi?* Želi da takav stav srca prati i cijelo večerašnje promišljanje.

Time pater Šujević ispovijed izvlači iz okvira rutine i obveze te je postavlja kao događaj u kojem se uvijek može primiti nešto novo.
sections.subtitle_en: Entering Confession with Imagination: The Sacrament as a Living Encounter with God
sections.screenshot_description_en: Father Sebastian Šujević invites those gathered to enter the sacrament of confession tonight with imagination
sections.content_en:
Father **Sebastian Šujević** opens the catechesis within the cycle of **DDV cateheses** on the budiFRAjer channel with a reminder of what man is endowed with: reason, intelligence, memory, free will, and a heart, but also **imagination**. It is precisely through all these faculties, he emphasizes, that the Lord reveals Himself, speaks to man, prompts him, and makes possible an encounter with Him.

The fundamental thought from which he starts is that **every sacrament is above all an encounter**, namely a "deep encounter with the living God." That is why he invites listeners to enter the sacrament of confession tonight precisely with imagination, with expectation, and openness. He suggests to them to carry a simple question in their heart: *what new thing will the Lord give me in the next confession?* He wants such an attitude of the heart to accompany the entire reflection tonight.

In doing so, Father Šujević pulls confession out of the framework of routine and obligation, presenting it as an event in which one can always receive something new.

sections.subtitle: Dva sina, dva lica grijeha: prispodoba koja sažima cijelu ispovijed
sections.screenshot_description: Pater Šujević opisuje proračunatost i hladnoću starijeg sina iz prispodobe
sections.content:
Kao širu perspektivu za razumijevanje ispovijedi pater Šujević uzima **prispodobu o milosrdnom Ocu, rasipnom sinu i starijem sinu**. Naglašava da je jedna ispovijed zapravo sažetak cijele te stvarnosti i cijeloga života likova iz evanđeoske priče.

Najprije podsjeća na **mlađeg sina**: punoljetan je, odlučio je uzeti ono što mu pripada i uvjeren je da zna kako će se ostvariti. Dosta mu je „muke“ i discipline koja je, kako pater primjećuje, vjerojatno upravo donijela red u njegov život. Želi sam. Završava tako da sve potrati, a tek kad doživi „blato“ uspijeva čuti Gospodina, prepoznaje stvari, vraća se i dobiva sve natrag.

Drugi način na koji se nešto događa u ljudskom srcu pater vidi u **starijem bratu**. „Nije ni on bajan“, kaže, jer se i u njemu dogodilo nešto čudno. Zamišlja njegovu računicu: neka mlađi ode, pa će sve ostalo pripasti njemu, jer ako se on drži svega, Otac će mu „sto posto, jedan kroz jedan“ prepisati sve. Razliku između braće sažima ovako:

- **stariji sin**: hladnoća i proračunatost
- **mlađi sin**: „divljaštvo“, potpuna inercija i život po načelu *kako mi se danas hoće živjeti*
sections.subtitle_en: Two Sons, Two Faces of Sin: The Parable That Summarizes the Entire Confession
sections.screenshot_description_en: Father Šujević describes the calculation and coldness of the older son from the parable
sections.content_en:
As a broader perspective for understanding confession, Father Šujević takes the **parable of the merciful Father, the prodigal son, and the older son**. He emphasizes that a single confession is actually a summary of that entire reality and the entire life of the characters from the Gospel story.

First, he recalls the **younger son**: he is of age, has decided to take what belongs to him, and is convinced he knows how to fulfill himself. He has had enough of the "drudgery" and discipline that, as the father notes, probably brought order into his life in the first place. He wants to be on his own. He ends up squandering everything, and only when he experiences the "mud" does he manage to hear the Lord, recognizes things, returns, and receives everything back.

The father sees another way in which something happens in the human heart in the **older brother**. "He isn't great either," he says, because something strange happened in him as well. He imagines his calculation: let the younger one leave, and everything else will belong to him, because if he sticks to everything, the Father will "one hundred percent, one to one" sign everything over to him. He summarizes the difference between the brothers like this:

- **older son**: coldness and calculation
- **younger son**: "wildness", complete inertia, and living according to the principle of *how I feel like living today*

sections.subtitle: Ispovijed kao malo uskrsnuće i nova prilika
sections.screenshot_description: Pater Šujević govori o privilegiji čovjeka koji iz ispovjedaonice izlazi kao novi, spašeni čovjek
sections.content:
Prispodoba završava **gozbom**, a upravo ta gozba, prema patru Šujeviću, sažima ono što se događa u ispovijedi. Taj motiv povezuje s promišljanjem o smrti i spasenju, temom koja je obilježila večer.

„Zamislite koliko smo mi privilegirani“, kaže. Čovjek može biti na putu smrti, dušu može opteretiti grijesima, slijepim ulicama i krivim odlukama, ali kad dođe na ispovijed i izađe van, on je **spašen čovjek, novi čovjek**. Pater to opisuje kao „jedno malo uskrsnuće“, još jednu novu priliku.

Poziva slušatelje da uđu u taj „radijus kretanja“ i da u svaku misao koju iznosi pokušaju smjestiti sebe i ono što se događa u njihovim životima. Katehezu, dakle, ne zamišlja kao teorijsko izlaganje, nego kao osobno ispitivanje savjesti.
sections.subtitle_en: Confession as a Little Resurrection and a New Chance
sections.screenshot_description_en: Father Šujević speaks of the privilege of a person who leaves the confessional as a new, saved person
sections.content_en:
The parable ends with a **banquet**, and according to Father Šujević, it is precisely this banquet that summarizes what happens in confession. He connects this motif with the reflection on death and salvation, a theme that marked the evening.

"Imagine how privileged we are," he says. A person can be on the path of death, can weigh down their soul with sins, dead ends, and wrong decisions, but when they come to confession and step outside, they are a **saved person, a new person**. The father describes this as "a little resurrection," another new chance.

He invites listeners to enter into that "radius of movement" and to try to place themselves and what is happening in their lives into every thought he presents. Thus, he does not envision the catechesis as a theoretical lecture, but as a personal examination of conscience.

sections.subtitle: Borba se vodi ondje gdje si najslabiji: gdje izgovaraš prvi „da“ grijehu
sections.screenshot_description: Pater Šujević objašnjava trenutak u kojem se odškrinu vrata i čovjek izgovara prvi „da“ grijehu
sections.content:
Pater Šujević ističe da se u prispodobi susreću tri srca: srce jednog sina, srce drugog sina i **srce Očevo**. U srcima obojice sinova odvija se borba, ali na vrlo različite načine. „Borbe su prilagođene tvojim slabostima“, objašnjava. Borba za spasenje, za život, za ostvarenje, za slobodu i ljepotu vlastitog života događa se upravo ondje gdje je čovjek slab i gdje sam ne može.

Kod **mlađeg sina** ta je borba **dinamična**: svaki je dan drugačiji i nikad se ne zna što će donijeti sutra. Kod **starijeg sina** sve je **pasivno**. Nekoliko tvrdih odluka blokira mu cijeli život. Te je odluke donio sam, ali pod utjecajem misli koje su dolazile od đavla ili iz vlastite sebičnosti i oholosti te su u jednom trenutku prevagnule nad dobrim poticajima Duha i anđela Božjih.

Iz toga izvodi konkretna pitanja za osobno promišljanje:

- Koja je tvoja najčešća borba, s čime se najviše mučiš?
- Koje su njezine okolnosti i što se tada događa?
- Koja je prva misao na putu do trenutka kad si zgriješio i odakle sve počinje?

Upravo tu se, kaže, „odškrinu vrata“, tu čovjek izgovara **prvi „da“** grijehu, odnosno misli koja se s njim poigrava, zavodi ga i manipulira njime jer poznaje njegovu slabost. Pater dodaje da svatko prolazi kroz faze i jednog i drugog sina, jer su ljudi „živa bića, živi organizmi, žive duše“. U tu borbu dolazi Gospodin, a čovjek je donosi u ispovijed.
sections.subtitle_en: The Battle Is Fought Where You Are Weakest: Where You Utter the First "Yes" to Sin
sections.screenshot_description_en: Father Šujević explains the moment when the door is cracked open and man utters the first "yes" to sin
sections.content_en:
Father Šujević points out that three hearts meet in the parable: the heart of one son, the heart of the other son, and the **Father's heart**. In the hearts of both sons, a battle takes place, but in very different ways. "Battles are tailored to your weaknesses," he explains. The battle for salvation, for life, for fulfillment, for freedom and the beauty of one's own life takes place precisely where man is weak and where he cannot do it on his own.

With the **younger son**, that battle is **dynamic**: every day is different and one never knows what tomorrow will bring. With the **older son**, everything is **passive**. A few rigid decisions block his entire life. He made those decisions on his own, but under the influence of thoughts that came from the devil or from his own selfishness and pride, and at one point they outweighed the good promptings of the Spirit and the angels of God.

From this, he derives concrete questions for personal reflection:

- What is your most frequent battle, what do you struggle with the most?
- What are its circumstances, and what happens then?
- What is the first thought on the way to the moment you sinned, and where does it all begin?

It is precisely there, he says, that "the door is cracked open," there man utters the **first "yes"** to sin, that is, to the thought that toys with him, seduces him, and manipulates him because it knows his weakness. The father adds that everyone goes through the phases of both sons, because people are "living beings, living organisms, living souls." Into that battle comes the Lord, and man brings it to confession.

sections.subtitle: Ispovjedaonica kao Očevo srce: Otac koji navija za tebe
sections.screenshot_description: Pater Šujević poziva vjernike da ulazak u ispovjedaonicu zamisle kao ulazak u Očevo srce
sections.content:
Na pitanje što se događa u ispovijedi pater Šujević odgovara: **susret Oca i Sina**. Usput primjećuje da ispovjedaonice te večeri „rade punom parom“ i poziva svakoga da ulazak u ispovjedaonicu zamisli kao **ulazak u Očevo srce**, gdje je čovjek sam i ima vremena sa svojim nebeskim Ocem.

Opisuje i put „od ispovijedi do ispovijedi“: čovjek proživljava ono što proživljava, dok ga Otac s druge strane **strpljivo, milosrdno i s ljubavlju** promatra i navija za njega. Taj stav dočarava primjerom Očeve molitve: *daj da Ivan prođe tu prepreku, daj da Ana uspije i ne nasjedne na varku koja je svaki mjesec zezne, pa da opet sama sebe povrijedi*.

Slušatelje pita imaju li i sami osjećaj da se to događa u njihovom životu. Bog, poručuje, ne promatra čovjekovu borbu kao hladni sudac, nego kao otac koji ga bodri.
sections.subtitle_en: The Confessional as the Father's Heart: The Father Who Cheers for You
sections.screenshot_description_en: Father Šujević invites the faithful to imagine entering the confessional as entering the Father's heart
sections.content_en:
To the question of what happens in confession, Father Šujević answers: **an encounter between Father and Son**. Along the way, he notices that the confessionals that evening are "working at full steam" and invites everyone to imagine entering the confessional as **entering the Father's heart**, where man is alone and has time with his heavenly Father.

He also describes the path "from confession to confession": man experiences what he experiences, while the Father on the other side **patiently, mercifully, and with love** observes him and cheers for him. He illustrates this attitude with the example of the Father's prayer: *let Ivan overcome that obstacle, let Ana succeed and not fall for the trick that messes her up every month, so that she hurts herself again*.

He asks the listeners if they themselves feel that this is happening in their lives. God, he says, does not observe man's struggle as a cold judge, but as a father who encourages him.

sections.subtitle: Zamka malodušja: „Zašto ići na ispovijed kad ću opet sagriješiti?“
sections.screenshot_description: Pater Šujević objašnjava da čovjek pada kad ide sam, a bit je u tome da sljedeći put ide s Isusom
sections.content:
Središnje pitanje večeri pater Šujević čuje i od ljudi koji mu dolaze: *zašto ići na ispovijed i kajati se ako ću, čim izađem van, opet sagriješiti isto?* Takvu misao naziva **zamkom** i plodom malodušja koje se „uvuče“ u čovjeka.

Poziva sve koji su to ikada rekli ili se time sami optužili da si to priznaju, slome tu misao i odreknu je se, jer je riječ o **varci**. „Ako ideš sam, naravno da ćeš pogriješiti i pasti opet, ali nije u tome bit“, objašnjava. Bit je u tome da čovjek sljedeći put ide **s Gospodinom, s Isusom**, jer ono što čovjeku nije moguće, Gospodinu jest.

Potkrepljuje to riječima **svetog Pavla**: „Kada sam slab, onda sam jak.“ Tumači ih ovako: kad je čovjek jak, on „ide, gazi, probija“ i ne mari puno, a kad je slab, pušta Isusa da bude s njim i zato je jak.

Zato onima koji su ispovjedniku govorili nešto poput „Pa pater, pa fra Stjepane, ja ću sutra opet to zgriješiti“ poručuje: **povuci tu riječ i obriši je iz svoga života**.
sections.subtitle_en: The Trap of Discouragement: "Why Go to Confession When I Will Sin Again?"
sections.screenshot_description_en: Father Šujević explains that man falls when he goes alone, and the point is to go with Jesus next time
sections.content_en:
The central question of the evening Father Šujević hears also from people who come to him: *why go to confession and repent if, as soon as I go outside, I will sin the same way again?* He calls such a thought a **trap** and the fruit of discouragement that "creeps" into a person.

He invites all who have ever said that or accused themselves with it to admit it to themselves, break that thought, and renounce it, because it is a **delusion**. "If you go alone, of course you will make a mistake and fall again, but that is not the point," he explains. The point is that next time man goes **with the Lord, with Jesus**, because what is not possible for man is possible for the Lord.

He supports this with the words of **Saint Paul**: "When I am weak, then I am strong." He interprets them like this: when man is strong, he "goes, tramples, breaks through" and does not care much, but when he is weak, he lets Jesus be with him, and therefore he is strong.

Therefore, to those who have said something to the confessor like "Well Father, well fra Stjepan, I will sin that again tomorrow," he says: **take back that word and erase it from your life**.

sections.subtitle: Put do ispovjedaonice: kava, kiša, gužva i glasovi koji odgovaraju
sections.screenshot_description: Pater Šujević slikovito nabraja izgovore i prepreke koje se pojave kad se netko odluči ispovjediti
sections.content:
Pater Šujević poziva slušatelje da se zapitaju kako se pripremaju za ispovijed, kako dolaze Gospodinu i što mu donose. Upozorava da, osim borbe do trenutka odluke, postoji i **druga borba**: ona od trenutka kad se čovjek odluči do trenutka kad zaista uđe u ispovjedaonicu.

Te prepreke opisuje vrlo životno:

- poziv na kavu baš na večer kad je odlučio ići na misu i ispovijed
- obveze za fakultet ili posao koje „moraju“ biti gotove sutra
- netko pred vratima tko „nešto treba“
- izgovori poput „kiša pada“, „ružno je vrijeme“, „bit će gužva i red“
- strah od toga tko ispovijeda i hoće li „opet naletjeti na nekoga“

Prepoznaje i glasove koji šapću da je to glupo, da čovjek može još izdržati, „još malo griješiti, još par dana, pa onda otići“. Svašta tada može doći, kaže, i dodaje: „ne da može, nego dolazi“. Ipak, sve to tumači kao **dobar znak** da je riječ o pravom trenutku susreta s Ocem nebeskim.

S druge strane, poziva da se prepoznaju i **dobri poticaji**. To može biti prijatelj ili prijateljica koji kaže: „Ajmo na ispovijed, prvi petak je“, ili poziv na duhovnu obnovu. Podsjeća i da se u **studenom** dobrom ispovijedi i molitvom za **potpuni oprost** može mnogo učiniti za duše u čistilištu, za vlastite pokojne i pokojne iz obitelji. Dobri poticaji dolaze, zaključuje, jer se Gospodin brine i bori za čovjeka.
sections.subtitle_en: The Way to the Confessional: Coffee, Rain, Crowds, and Voices That Talk Back
sections.screenshot_description_en: Father Šujević vividly lists the excuses and obstacles that appear when someone decides to go to confession
sections.content_en:
Father Šujević invites listeners to ask themselves how they prepare for confession, how they come to the Lord, and what they bring to Him. He warns that, besides the battle leading up to the moment of decision, there is also a **second battle**: the one from the moment a person decides until the moment they actually enter the confessional.

He describes these obstacles very realistically:

- an invitation for coffee on the very evening when one decided to go to Mass and confession
- obligations for university or work that "must" be finished tomorrow
- someone at the door who "needs something"
- excuses like "it's raining," "the weather is bad," "there will be a crowd and a line"
- fear of who is hearing confessions and whether one will "run into someone again"

He also recognizes voices whispering that it is stupid, that one can hold out a bit longer, "sin a little more, a few more days, and then go." All sorts of things can come up then, he says, and adds: "not that it can, but it does come." Yet, he interprets all of this as a **good sign** that it is the right moment for an encounter with the heavenly Father.

On the other hand, he calls for recognizing **good promptings** as well. That can be a male or female friend who says: "Let's go to confession, it's First Friday," or an invitation to a spiritual retreat. He also reminds that in **November**, through a good confession and prayer for a **plenary indulgence**, much can be done for the souls in purgatory, for one's own deceased, and deceased family members. Good promptings come, he concludes, because the Lord cares and fights for man.

sections.subtitle: Zagrljaj, nova haljina, prsten i sandale: što se zbiva u ispovjedaonici
sections.screenshot_description: Pater Šujević citira evanđelje o Ocu koji se zaletio, bacio sinu oko vrata, izgrlio ga i izljubio
sections.content:
Kako bi odgovorio na pitanje što se događa u ispovjedaonici, pater Šujević se ponovno vraća prispodobi. Otac je sina ugledao izdaleka. Možda nije imao dvogled kao danas, ali je iščekivao, borio se i molio da se sin vrati. Pater dopušta mogućnost da je i otac u prispodobi iz vlastitog iskustva znao što znači otići i „zaglibiti“, pa je zato još žarče iščekivao.

Evanđelje kaže da se otac „zaletio, bacio mu se oko vrata, izgrlio ga i izljubio“. „Tako tebe Bog čeka u ispovjedaonici“, poručuje pater. Tako ga voli i tako žarko čezne da dođe.

Zatim tumači simbole darova koje otac daje sinu:

- **nova bijela haljina**: nova duša, novo srce
- **prsten na ruci**: vraćena baština i identitet slobodnog djeteta Božjeg
- **sandale na nogama**: snaga za put, „da te više ne ranjavaju iste stvari, da ne krvariš“, nego da budeš osposobljen ostvariti se

„To je jedna ispovijed“, zaključuje. Dodaje da tako ne gleda samo Otac nebeski, nego i anđeli, posebno **anđeo čuvar**, koji čovjeka neprestano nagovara i bori se da uđe u ispovjedaonicu, kako bi mu ta ispovijed postala susret oslobođenja.
sections.subtitle_en: An Embrace, a New Robe, a Ring, and Sandals: What Takes Place in the Confessional
sections.screenshot_description_en: Father Šujević quotes the Gospel about the Father who ran, threw his arms around his son's neck, embraced him, and kissed him
sections.content_en:
In order to answer the question of what happens in the confessional, Father Šujević returns again to the parable. The father saw the son from afar. Perhaps he did not have binoculars like today, but he was waiting, fighting, and praying for the son to return. The father allows for the possibility that the father in the parable also knew from his own experience what it meant to leave and "get bogged down," so he waited even more fervently.

The Gospel says that the father "ran, threw himself around his neck, embraced him, and kissed him." "That is how God waits for you in the confessional," says the father. That is how He loves him and so ardently longs for him to come.

Then he interprets the symbols of the gifts the father gives to the son:

- **new white robe**: a new soul, a new heart
- **ring on the hand**: restored heritage and identity of a free child of God
- **sandals on the feet**: strength for the journey, "so that the same things no longer wound you, so that you do not bleed," but rather that you are equipped to fulfill yourself

"That is a single confession," he concludes. He adds that not only does the heavenly Father look at it that way, but also the angels, especially the **guardian angel**, who constantly urges man and fights for him to enter the confessional, so that this confession becomes an encounter of liberation for him.

sections.subtitle: Prvi korak dobre ispovijedi: vjerovati da Bog doista sve briše
sections.screenshot_description: Pater Šujević ističe da je prvi korak vjera da Bog u ispovijedi sve oprašta i više nikad ne proziva
sections.content:
Pater Šujević zatim donosi nekoliko koraka koji pomažu ostvariti dobru ispovijed i dublje „kušati“ Božju ljubav. Objašnjava da se to događalo i mlađem sinu te da se događa i u svakome čovjeku, „ovisno u kojem obujmu“. Kad čovjek zna kako se pripremiti, može dublje iskoristiti Božju milost i svjesnije ući u blagodati ispovijedi.

**Prvi korak je vjera.** Vjernik treba vjerovati da mu se u ispovjedaonici sve oprašta, da Bog sve briše i da ga više nikad neće prozvati riječima: *tad i tad si to zgriješio, dođi mi dati zadovoljštinu*. Isto tako, Bog mu nakon ispovijedi neće reći da više nije njegov sin ili kći zato što je zgriješio. Za Boga je, naglašava pater, uvijek isti i uvijek prima istu ljubav.

Pater priznaje da se može javiti i sumnja: *otkupljuje li me Bog u ispovijedi doista i prihvaća li me takvog kakav jesam?* Ispovijed vjernika upravo zato izaziva da obnovi vjeru i ispovjedi je: „Bog me otkupljuje, Bog me liječi, Bog me iscjeljuje, Bog mi oprašta.“ Po ispovijedi čovjek postaje **novi čovjek**.
sections.subtitle_en: The First Step of a Good Confession: Believing That God Truly Erases Everything
sections.screenshot_description_en: Father Šujević emphasizes that the first step is faith that God forgives everything in confession and never brings it up again
sections.content_en:
Father Šujević then brings forward several steps that help achieve a good confession and more deeply "taste" God's love. He explains that this also happened to the younger son and that it happens in every person, "depending on the extent." When a person knows how to prepare, they can more deeply utilize God's grace and enter more consciously into the benefits of confession.

**The first step is faith.** The believer needs to believe that in the confessional everything is forgiven him, that God erases everything and will never again call him out with the words: *at such and such a time you committed that sin, come give me satisfaction*. Likewise, God will not tell him after confession that he is no longer His son or daughter because he sinned. For God, the father emphasizes, he is always the same and always receives the same love.

The father admits that doubt can also arise: *does God truly redeem me in confession and accept me as I am?* Confession therefore challenges the believer precisely to renew faith and confess it: "God redeems me, God heals me, God restores me, God forgives me." Through confession, man becomes a **new man**.

> "Magisterium alignment:"
> The teaching that God completely forgives and remits the guilt of mortal sins in the sacrament of penance is fully consistent with Catholic doctrine (CCC 1468-1470). Temporal punishment may remain, which is satisfied through penance and indulgences.

sections.subtitle: Oprostiti i tražiti oprost: „Nema bez oprosta“
sections.screenshot_description: Pater Šujević objašnjava da ispovijed traži da čovjek oprosti drugima i sam zatraži oprost
sections.content:
**Drugi korak** prema patru Šujeviću jest opraštanje. Ispovijed od čovjeka traži da i sam oprosti onima koji su se o njega ogriješili: koji su ga povrijedili, izdali, iznevjerili, nanijeli mu nepravdu, osramotili ga ili se s njim posvađali, „što god bilo“.

Vrijedi i obrnuto: čovjek treba **tražiti oprost** za ono što je sam učinio drugima. Pater ističe da je ponekad važno to učiniti **uživo**, licem u lice s onima koje je povrijedio. Ponekad to Gospodin jednostavno zahtijeva, a duh u čovjeku mu „ne da mira“ dok ne ode i ne kaže: *Oprosti mi, stvarno sam tu pogriješio, stvarno sam tu zabrljala.*

„Nije to lako, ali nakon toga si jači čovjek“, kaže. Podsjeća koliko puta Isus u evanđeljima ponavlja važnost opraštanja te parafrazira njegovu poruku: *nemoj mi dolaziti na oltar ako nisi oprostio ili zatražio oprost.* Zaključak je jasan: **nema bez oprosta**.
sections.subtitle_en: To Forgive and Ask for Forgiveness: "There Is None Without Forgiveness"
sections.screenshot_description_en: Father Šujević explains that confession requires man to forgive others and ask for forgiveness himself
sections.content_en:
**The second step**, according to Father Šujević, is forgiving. Confession requires man to forgive those who have sinned against him as well: who have hurt him, betrayed him, failed him, wronged him, shamed him, or quarreled with him, "whatever it may be."

The reverse is also true: man needs to **ask for forgiveness** for what he himself has done to others. The father emphasizes that sometimes it is important to do this **in person**, face to face with those he has hurt. Sometimes the Lord simply demands this, and the spirit within man "gives him no peace" until he goes and says: *Forgive me, I really made a mistake here, I really messed up here.*

"It is not easy, but after that you are a stronger person," he says. He recalls how many times Jesus repeats the importance of forgiveness in the Gospels and paraphrases His message: *do not come to my altar if you have not forgiven or asked for forgiveness.* The conclusion is clear: **there is none without forgiveness**.

sections.subtitle: „Mrzim na sve svoje grijehe“: lažna slatkoća grijeha i „šugavi“ mobitel
sections.screenshot_description: Pater Šujević govori o ovisnosti o mobitelu, skrolanju i praznini koja ostaje na kraju
sections.content:
Sljedeći korak pater Šujević smatra posebno zanimljivim: **odriče li se čovjek doista grijeha s kojim se bori?** Upozorava na „sitnicu“ koju vjernici često ne primijete kad mole **čin pokajanja**. U njemu stoji: „Kajem se od svega srca što sam uvrijedio Boga, svoje najveće i najmilije dobro“, a zatim i: „**Mrzim na sve svoje grijehe.**“

Vjeruje da većina koristi upravo tu molitvu, ali onima koji još mole kraći, dječji čin pokajanja iz vremena prve pričesti savjetuje da ga zamijene ovim, jer je „malo dublji“ i više zaokuplja.

Zatim pita: *mrziš li te grijehe?* Poziva da se svatko prisjeti zbog čega je zgriješio, jer je u igri uvijek neka **lažna slatkoća grijeha**, zadovoljenje nekog užitka. Taj užitak može biti:

- materijalan ili tjelesni
- duhovni, primjerice osjećaj pobjede ili uzdizanja nad drugim
- užitak **mobitela**: skrolanje i „buđenje endorfina, dopamina i ne znam svega čega, a na koncu praznina“

„Ali opet uzimaš taj mobitel šugavi“, slikovito dodaje. Spominje i neumjerenost, bludnost i ogovaranje, nakon kojih čovjek bude „sam sebi smrdljiv“ i na kraju uvidi da je sve to „stvarno glupo“.

Pater zato zaključuje da su **odricanje i mržnja na grijeh legitimni**. Čovjek se smije i treba odreći grijeha, jer to i izgovara u ispovijedi, pa neka zato pripremi srce da to bude izrečeno s vjerom i uvjerenjem. Odricanjem od grijeha i zloga čovjek kao da je „zalupio vrata“ onome koji ga želi ubiti duhom i strovaliti u pakao te je prerezao sve veze s njim. Tako povlači onaj prvi „da“ koji je dao grijehu.
sections.subtitle_en: "I Hate All My Sins": The False Sweetness of Sin and the "Lousy" Cell Phone
sections.screenshot_description_en: Father Šujević talks about addiction to the cell phone, scrolling, and the emptiness that remains at the end
sections.content_en:
Father Šujević considers the next step particularly interesting: **does man truly renounce the sin he is fighting against?** He warns of a "detail" that the faithful often do not notice when praying the **act of contrition**. In it, it states: "I am heartily sorry for having offended God, my greatest and dearest good," and then also: "**I hate all my sins.**"

He believes that the majority uses precisely this prayer, but to those who still pray the shorter, children's act of contrition from the time of First Communion, he advises replacing it with this one, because it is "a little deeper" and engages more.

Then he asks: *do you hate those sins?* He calls everyone to remember why they sinned, because at play is always some **false sweetness of sin**, the satisfaction of some pleasure. That pleasure can be:

- material or bodily
- spiritual, for example a feeling of victory or elevation over another
- the pleasure of the **cell phone**: scrolling and "the awakening of endorphins, dopamine, and I don't know what all, and in the end emptiness"

"Yet you pick up that lousy cell phone again," he vividly adds. He also mentions intemperance, lust, and gossip, after which man finds himself "foul-smelling to himself" and in the end realizes that all of it is "really stupid."

The father therefore concludes that **renunciation and hatred of sin are legitimate**. Man may and should renounce sin, because he utters that in confession, so let him prepare his heart for it to be spoken with faith and conviction. By renouncing sin and the evil one, it is as though man has "slammed the door" on the one who wants to kill him in spirit and plunge him into hell, and has severed all ties with him. Thus he retracts that first "yes" he gave to sin.

sections.subtitle: „Gospodine, došao sam po svoju slobodu“
sections.screenshot_description: Pater Šujević potiče vjernike da na ispovijed dođu sa sviješću da dolaze po svoju slobodu
sections.content:
Kao još jedan korak koji može pomoći pater Šujević navodi **želju za slobodom**. Sloboda, kaže, nije tek dodatak, nego čovjekov **identitet**: on je *slobodno dijete Božje*.

Zato savjetuje da vjernik na ispovijed dođe svjestan da je došao po svoju slobodu, i da to Gospodinu izravno kaže: *Gospodine, došao sam po svoju slobodu.* Pritom treba imenovati i od čega točno želi biti oslobođen.

Ovaj korak nadovezuje se na simboliku prstena iz prispodobe, kojim Otac sinu vraća baštinu i dostojanstvo slobodnog djeteta.
sections.screenshot_description_en: Father Šujević encourages the faithful to come to confession with the awareness that they are coming for their freedom
sections.content_en:
As another step that can help, Father Šujević cites the **desire for freedom**. Freedom, he says, is not merely an addition, but man's **identity**: he is a *free child of God*.

Therefore, he advises that the believer come to confession aware that he has come for his freedom, and say that directly to the Lord: *Lord, I came for my freedom.* In doing so, he should also name what exactly he wants to be freed from.

This step builds on the symbolism of the ring from the parable, with which the Father restores to the son the heritage and dignity of a free child.

sections.subtitle: Odrješenje: Duh Sveti, otpuštenje grijeha i mir
sections.screenshot_description: Pater Šujević izgovara formulu odrješenja i tumači njezine tri ključne točke
sections.content:
„Najljepša stvar u ispovijedi je odrješenje“, ističe pater Šujević. To je trenutak u kojem Otac nebeski, kao u prispodobi, grli i ljubi čovjeka te mu daruje sve što je darovao sinu. U to vjernik treba biti uvjeren.

Preporučuje da se osvijesti **formula odrješenja**. Ne sviđa mu se kad je neki svećenici izmole u sebi ili izgovore samo njezin kraj, kao ni kad pokornici čin pokajanja mole u sebi. Takvima kaže: *Ne, lijepo na glas, neka te čuje Gospodin.* Izgovorene riječi, objašnjava, imaju svoju snagu i ljepotu. Zatim navodi formulu: „Bog, milosrdni Otac, pomirio je sa sobom svijet smrću i uskrsnućem svoga Sina. Izlio je Duha Svetoga za otpuštenje grijeha. Neka ti po služenju Crkve On udijeli oproštenje i mir.“

Vjernicima „stavlja na srce“ **tri točke** koje trebaju željeti i primati u što većoj snazi:

1. **Izlijevanje Duha Svetoga**: dok svećenik podiže ruku, Duh Sveti se izlijeva na pokornika, obnavlja krsnu milost i sve što je u njemu narušeno te stvara novi sklad.
2. **Otpuštenje grijeha**: po to je većina došla, „ma kako bio umoran, rastrojen“.
3. **Mir**: pater ga opisuje kao puninu Duha Svetoga, kao slobodu, iscjeljenje i ozdravljenje, ali i kao osnaživanje za životni put, zvanje i ostvarenje, za lijepe trenutke, ali i za nošenje križa. Ti su trenuci, naglašava, nezaobilazan dio života.

Zato poziva da vjernik bude svjestan što se tada događa i što želi. Gospodin dolazi potvrditi njegov identitet, iscijeliti ga ondje gdje je slab i ranjen te mu dati sve što mu treba za životni put, poslanje i poziv, za ostvarenje života na zemlji i za prelazak u nebo.
sections.subtitle_en: Absolution: The Holy Spirit, the Remission of Sins, and Peace
sections.screenshot_description_en: Father Šujević pronounces the formula of absolution and interprets its three key points
sections.content_en:
"The most beautiful thing in confession is absolution," emphasizes Father Šujević. That is the moment in which the heavenly Father, as in the parable, embraces and kisses man and grants him everything he granted to the son. Of this the believer should be convinced.

He recommends becoming aware of the **formula of absolution**. He does not like it when some priests pray it silently or utter only its conclusion, nor when penitents pray the act of contrition silently. To such people he says: *No, out loud nicely, let the Lord hear you.* The spoken words, he explains, have their own power and beauty. Then he quotes the formula: "God, the Father of mercies, through the death and resurrection of his Son has reconciled the world to himself and sent the Holy Spirit among us for the forgiveness of sins; through the ministry of the Church may God give you pardon and peace."

To the faithful he "lays upon their hearts" **three points** that they should desire and receive in the greatest possible power:

1. **The outpouring of the Holy Spirit**: as the priest raises his hand, the Holy Spirit is poured out upon the penitent, renewing baptismal grace and everything that has been damaged within him, creating a new harmony.
2. **The remission of sins**: this is what most have come for, "no matter how tired, distraught one may be."
3. **Peace**: the father describes it as the fullness of the Holy Spirit, as freedom, healing, and restoration, but also as empowerment for the life journey, vocation, and fulfillment, for beautiful moments, but also for carrying the cross. These moments, he emphasizes, are an unavoidable part of life.

Therefore, he calls for the believer to be aware of what is happening then and what he desires. The Lord comes to confirm his identity, heal him where he is weak and wounded, and give him everything he needs for the life path, mission, and vocation, for the fulfillment of life on earth and for the transition into heaven.

sections.subtitle: Sve u pet minuta: srce od kamena postaje srce od mesa
sections.screenshot_description: Pater Šujević naglašava da sve to može stati u jednu ispovijed od pet minuta
sections.content:
„To je sve jedna ispovijed od pet minuta. Sve ovo može tu stati“, kaže pater Šujević. Objašnjava to riječju da je za Gospodina tisuću godina kao jedan dan, a jedan dan kao tisuću godina.

U ispovijedi se, prema njegovim riječima, ispunjava obećanje iz **proroka Ezekiela**: „Uzet ću vaše srce kameno (…) i dat ću vam srce od mesa, nov duh udahnut ću u vas.“ Srce je postalo kameno zbog udaraca, zbog svega što se događa u životu, a možda i zbog nekih vlastitih odluka. U ispovijedi se to obećanje obnavlja i ostvaruje uvijek iznova.

Zatim najavljuje nekoliko primjera, uz obrazloženje: „Primjeri su ono što bude vjeru.“
sections.subtitle_en: Everything in Five Minutes: A Heart of Stone Becomes a Heart of Flesh
sections.screenshot_description_en: Father Šujević emphasizes that all of this can fit into a single five-minute confession
sections.content_en:
"That is all a five-minute confession. All of this can fit in there," says Father Šujević. He explains this with the saying that for the Lord a thousand years are like one day, and a day like a thousand years.

In confession, according to his words, the promise from the **prophet Ezekiel** is fulfilled: "I will remove the heart of stone from you (…) and give you a heart of flesh, a new spirit I will put within you." The heart became stone because of blows, because of everything that happens in life, and perhaps because of some personal decisions. In confession, that promise is renewed and fulfilled over and over again.

Then he announces a few examples, with the explanation: "Examples are what awaken faith."

sections.subtitle: Osobno svjedočanstvo sa Zameta: fratar, Psalam 103 i suze slobode
sections.screenshot_description: Pater Šujević prisjeća se ispovijedi kod fratra na obnovi za mlade na Zametu u Rijeci
sections.content:
Pater Šujević priznaje da je **najviše milosti od svih sakramenata** primio upravo u ispovijedi, i prije nego što je postao svećenik i danas. Posebno je doživljava kao iscjeljenje, ohrabrenje, utjehu i snagu u svemu što čovjek proživljava.

Prisjeća se jedne obnove u **Rijeci**, odakle je rodom, na **Zametu**, gdje je bila organizirana ispovijed za mlade. Bio je otprilike na prvoj godini studija. Kaže da mu je već bila „puna kapa svega“, jer su se vraćali isti grijesi, „kao i svakom mladom čovjeku većinom“. Otišao je na ispovijed kod jednog fratra.

Ispovijed je, kako kaže, bila „ništa posebno“: vrlo jednostavna, puna suosjećanja, mira i radosti. Za pokoru je dobio molitvu **Psalma 103**. Kad ga je izmolio, uslijedile su suze, toplina u srcu i „napokon sloboda“, a s njima ohrabrenje i rasterećenje. „Ovih stvari više nema“, prisjeća se, i opisuje to kao novo, jednostavno stanje.
sections.subtitle_en: Personal Testimony from Zamet: A Friar, Psalm 103, and Tears of Freedom
sections.screenshot_description_en: Father Šujević recalls a confession with a friar at a youth retreat at Zamet in Rijeka
sections.content_en:
Father Šujević admits that he received the **most graces of all the sacraments** precisely in confession, both before he became a priest and today. He experiences it especially as healing, encouragement, comfort, and strength in everything a person goes through.

He recalls a retreat in **Rijeka**, where he is originally from, at **Zamet**, where confession was organized for young people. He was approximately in his first year of college. He says that he was already "fed up with everything," because the same sins kept returning, "as with most young people." He went to confession with a friar.

The confession was, as he says, "nothing special": very simple, full of compassion, peace, and joy. For penance, he was given the prayer of **Psalm 103**. When he prayed it, tears followed, warmth in the heart, and "finally freedom," and with them encouragement and relief. "These things are no more," he recalls, and describes it as a new, simple state.

sections.subtitle: Oslobođenje od ovisnosti i nemira nakon prizivanja duhova
sections.screenshot_description: Pater Šujević pripovijeda o mladiću koji je tijekom prizivanja duhova kapnuo krv na svijeću
sections.content:
Kao svećenik, pater Šujević svjedočio je sličnim iskustvima kod drugih. Dok je mogao više raditi s ljudima i pripremati ih za ispovijed, susretao je **ovisnike o drogi i pornografiji** koji su uz dobru pripremu doživjeli oslobođenje. Nakon ispovijedi, kaže, nestao je nagon, ta „pokvarena strast“ više nije vladala. Napasti i dalje postoje, ali je **odnos snaga sasvim drugačiji**.

Zatim pripovijeda priču koja, kako kaže, „ide i uz ove dane“. Zvale su ga časne sestre jer je na duhovnoj obnovi bio mladić s problemima, pa su ga zamolile da dođe ranije. Mladić nije mogao spavati, bio je posve iscrpljen i doveli su ga na obnovu ravno s infuzije. U sebi je osjećao velik nemir, a uzrok je bilo **prizivanje duhova**.

Skupina mladih pronašla je staru kuću kako bi ondje prizivala duhove. Jedan ih je vodio i imao čak bilježnicu s uputama. U jednom je trenutku trebalo kapnuti krv na svijeću, a mladić se javio da to učini. Ubo se iglom, kapnuo krv i, prema patrovim riječima, u tom mu se trenutku promijenio život: nije mogao spavati, osjećao je neku čudnu prisutnost i nemir. Kad bi došao u crkvu, bilo bi mu još gore, pa je morao izlaziti van.

Rješenje je bilo vrlo jednostavno i slijedilo je korake o kojima je pater govorio: **odricanje, ispovijed, vjerovanje**. Nakon toga mladić je bio potpuno slobodan i sretan te je ministrirao. Pater mu je rekao da ga nazove ako se problem vrati. „Nije više zvao“, zaključuje, i dodaje: „Jedna ispovijed, kolike čudesne stvari u sebi sadrži.“
sections.subtitle_en: Deliverance from Addiction and Restlessness After Necromancy
sections.screenshot_description_en: Father Šujević recounts a young man who dripped blood onto a candle during a séance
sections.content_en:
As a priest, Father Šujević has witnessed similar experiences in others. While he was able to work more with people and prepare them for confession, he met **drug and pornography addicts** who, with good preparation, experienced liberation. After confession, he says, the urge disappeared, that "corrupted passion" no longer ruled. Temptations still exist, but the **balance of power is completely different**.

Then he narrates a story that, as he says, "goes with these days as well." Religious sisters called him because at a spiritual retreat there was a young man with problems, so they asked him to come earlier. The young man could not sleep, was completely exhausted, and they brought him to the retreat straight from an IV drip. Inside, he felt great restlessness, and the cause was **invoking spirits**.

A group of young people found an old house in order to invoke spirits there. One of them led them and even had a notebook with instructions. At one point, blood had to be dripped onto a candle, and the young man volunteered to do it. He pricked himself with a needle, dripped blood, and, according to the father's words, at that moment his life changed: he could not sleep, felt some strange presence and restlessness. Whenever he came to church, he felt even worse, so he had to go outside.

The solution was very simple and followed the steps the father spoke about: **renunciation, confession, believing**. After that, the young man was completely free and happy and served at the altar. The father told him to call him if the problem returned. "He didn't call anymore," he concludes, and adds: "A single confession, what wondrous things it contains within itself."

sections.subtitle: Mir sakramenta, Psalam 103 i ispovijed kao vrata prema euharistiji
sections.screenshot_description: Pater Šujević na kraju kateheze čita Psalam 103
sections.content:
Na kraju pater Šujević ponovno govori o **miru** koji se po sakramentu spušta na čovjeka i daje mu sve što mu treba za život. Poziva slušatelje da razaberu što je upravo njima potrebno, bilo radost ili više sigurnosti. Ako ih muči osjećaj manje vrijednosti, krivnje, nesposobnosti, straha ili tjeskobe, neka to donesu Gospodinu i puste ga da s tim radi, da „mijesi“ i učini njihovo srce novim i radosnim.

„Daj mu svoje pouzdanje“, ponavlja dvaput. Ako je Gospodin igdje prisutan, kaže, u sakramentu je prisutan **100 posto**, i ta prisutnost **ne ovisi o čovjekovu raspoloženju**.

Kako bi i slušatelji doživjeli nešto od onoga što je sam iskusio, pater čita **Psalam 103**: „Blagoslivljaj Gospodina, dušo moja, i sve što je u meni, sveto ime njegovo (…) On ti otpušta sve grijehe tvoje, on iscjeljuje sve slabosti tvoje (…) Ne postupa s nama po grijesima našim, niti nam plaća po našim krivnjama (…) Kako je istok daleko od zapada, tako udaljuje od nas bezakonja naša. Kako se otac smiluje dječici, tako se Gospodin smiluje onima što ga se boje.“

Katehezu zaključuje željom da i sljedeća ispovijed slušateljima otvori vrata „ovog čudesnog sakramenta“ i donese ljepotu koju će otkrivati cijeli život, malo-pomalo. Priznaje da i sam kao svećenik i danas u njoj otkriva uvijek nešto novo. Nagrada je, kaže, **euharistija** i klanjanje koje slijedi, mjesto na kojem Otac vjernike „pečati kao svoju djecu“.
sections.subtitle_en: The Peace of the Sacrament, Psalm 103, and Confession as the Gate to the Eucharist
sections.screenshot_description_en: Father Šujević reads Psalm 103 at the end of the catechesis
sections.content_en:
At the end, Father Šujević speaks again about the **peace** that descends upon man through the sacrament and gives him everything he needs for life. He invites listeners to discern what is needed precisely for them, whether joy or more security. If they are troubled by feelings of inadequacy, guilt, incompetence, fear, or anxiety, let them bring that to the Lord and let Him work with it, let Him "knead" and make their heart new and joyful.

"Give Him your trust," he repeats twice. If the Lord is present anywhere, he says, He is present in the sacrament **100 percent**, and that presence **does not depend on man's mood**.

So that the listeners would also experience something of what he himself experienced, the father reads **Psalm 103**: "Bless the Lord, O my soul, and all that is within me, bless his holy name (…) He forgives all your iniquities, he heals all your infirmities (…) He does not deal with us according to our sins, nor repay us according to our iniquities (…) As far as the east is from the west, so far does he remove our transgressions from us. As a father shows compassion to his children, so the Lord shows compassion to those who fear him."

He concludes the catechesis with the wish that the next confession also opens the door of "this wondrous sacrament" to listeners and brings beauty that they will discover throughout their entire life, little by little. He admits that even today as a priest he always discovers something new in it. The reward is, he says, the **Eucharist** and the Eucharistic adoration that follows, the place where the Father "seals believers as His children."

iterations.theme_en: Why Go to Confession if You Will Sin Again? Catechesis by Father Sebastian Šujević on the Sacrament of Confession as an Encounter with the Merciful Father
